newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran expects to raise cement exports.
newsitem.headline: Iran expects to raise cement exports.

text.p: Iran expects to export two million tonnes of cement in the year to March 1998, up from 665,000 tonnes the previous year, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.
Industry Minister Mohammad Reza Nematzadeh said exports of two million tonnes would be reached after new cement plants come onstream in the Iranian year to March 20, 1998, IRNA said.
Iran said last month 665,000 tonnes of cement worth $20 million were exported during the last Iranian year.
Nematzadeh was speaking in the Gulf port city of Bandar Abbas at the opening of the first unit of a cement plant with a daily production capacity of 3,000 tonnes, IRNA said.
The plant has so far cost $110 million in hard currency in addition to 250 billion rials ($83.3 million) to build, it said.
Once completed, the second unit of the project would produce another 3,000 tons of cement a day, it added.
Iran has said cement production was expected to rise to 30 million tonnes by the end of March 1999 from 18.5 million tonnes in the last Iranian year ending March 1997.
Iran in October temporarily banned exports of cement and announced new rules governing its distribution to counter a surge in prices which local press reports blamed on shortages and profiteering.

In late 1994, Tehran said it planned to become a major regional cement exporter by raising annual output to 25 million tonnes within two years. But some officials later said financial problems had delayed several cement plants from coming onstream.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
